University of Oxford
United Kingdom · DPhil in Mathematics; MSc in Mathematical Sciences (OMMS)
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• No separate CV upload: Oxford removes it.
• DPhil funding deadline is nearly two months before the expected final academic deadline.
• No automatic English waiver: request it; current TOEFL format restriction matters if waiver is refused.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [2027 confirmed]
Both programmes accept an appropriate first-class-equivalent bachelor’s; the normal minimum for a US degree
is 3.7/4.0. A master’s is not categorically required for the DPhil. A UChicago mathematics bachelor’s can
therefore meet the degree-route requirement, conditional on grades, preparation and completion before entry.
F-1 status is not a nationality or funding entitlement. DPhil 3-4 years; OMMS nine months. Both begin 4 October
2027. [a] [b]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select DPhil versus OMMS and create the Oxford graduate application. DPhil: name at least one research group
in the proposed-field section; up to three supervisors may be suggested, without prior approval. OMMS: choose
a preferred subject grouping; Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory, Topology and Logic is the closest initial
choice and does not bind later options. Register three referees; request English waiver in the form; prepare
transcripts and the programme-specific statement. [a] [b] [c] [d]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
DPhil applicants need not obtain a supervisor’s agreement before applying; up to three names may be
suggested and academic contact is permitted. OMMS does not require a prospective supervisor. Current
rosters list Wiles, Kirwan, Hitchin and several historically prominent names as emeritus; do not treat them as
ordinary new-supervisor options without confirmation. The faculty below are a research-fit shortlist, not a
guarantee of 2027 availability. [a] [b] [p] [q] [r]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use Oxford’s online form and Applicant Self Service. Register referees before submission if desired; track
receipt after submission. Required documents use PDF/JPG/PNG and normal 4 MB maximum. Do not upload a
CV where the course forbids it. Live unpublished form questions and already-submitted-reference replacement
behavior remain unverified. [d] [e] [f] [g]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Both course pages explicitly publish 2027-28 entry dates and deadlines. General mechanics are standing
guidance. The stated scholarship-rate figures are prior-year examples, not 2027-28 promises. [a] [b] [k] [l]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
DPhil: 6 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time is the funding deadline; expected final deadline 2 March 2027 at
12:00 noon UK time, subject to places. OMMS: final deadline 27 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time. These are
midday, not midnight. [a] [b]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
DPhil funding consideration: 6 January 2027 noon UK. OMMS funding consideration: 27 January 2027 noon UK.
Clarendon automatically considers eligible course applications received by the relevant December/January
course deadline; other awards can impose their own deadlines. [a] [b] [k] [n]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
Register three referees. The application can become ready for assessment with two references received by the
relevant course deadline; Oxford may require the third before completing review. For safety request all three
by DPhil 6 January 2027 noon UK or OMMS 27 January 2027 noon UK when seeking funding. The deadline
entered by the applicant appears in the invitation and does not extend Oxford’s deadline. [a] [b] [d] [e]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
No GRE scores are sought. English evidence need not necessarily accompany the initial application: if a waiver
is refused, the individual offer specifies the condition and deadline. No universal 2027 test-score deadline was
established. [a] [b] [c] [m]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All required application materials must arrive by the selected course deadline, except English evidence where
permitted as a later offer condition. Submit early enough to correct format/missing-document problems.
Final-degree and other offer conditions have individualized deadlines. [a] [b] [c] [g] [m]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The department’s offer specifies the acceptance deadline and conditions; no uniform US-style April 15
commitment deadline applies. College financial declarations can have a separate deadline. [m]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
DPhil uses standard English: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 each component. OMMS uses higher
English: IELTS 7.5 overall, at least 7.0 each. Published TOEFL thresholds are 100 and 110 respectively, each
requiring listening 22, reading 24, speaking 25, writing 24, BUT both current course pages say TOEFL tests
taken from 21 January 2026 are not accepted pending review of the revised test. Consult the current official
table before booking. [a] [b]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A waiver can be requested for a completed or current full-time degree of at least nine months taught and
assessed entirely in English, with no more than two academic years between completion and Oxford entry.
UChicago falls within the US/majority-English-country route: additional medium-of-instruction evidence is not
normally required. Select the waiver request in the Languages section; the department decides, so it is not an
automatic exemption. Completion of the qualifying degree can be a condition. [c]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Neither course seeks GRE or GMAT scores. No separate Mathematics Subject Test requirement is listed; do not
add unsolicited scores as a substitute for the stated materials. [a] [b]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
DPhil: three referees, preferably academic; up to one professional reference can be accepted. OMMS: three, at
least two academic. In both cases Oxford may begin assessment with two received, while retaining the right to
require the third. [a] [b] [d]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Clarendon requires no separate application documents or references. Other named scholarships can require
additional material; citizenship-specific awards cannot be fully resolved without nationality. No universal
supplementary scholarship-reference requirement applies. [k] [n]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Registering a referee sends an email invitation immediately. Use institutional/professional email where
possible and enter a realistic deadline. The referee completes short questions and uploads a PDF reference. [e]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not held until application submission. The application may be submitted before references
arrive; each course application requires its own registered references. [d] [e]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Applicant Self Service displays reference status; Oxford emails the applicant when a reference is received. The
referee receives on-screen and email confirmation after submitting. [e] [f]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Self Service permits referee changes/additions and reminder/resend actions subject to the application state.
References must be registered/submitted separately for each application. Whether a submitted letter can be
replaced by the referee was not established publicly: ask graduate admissions before relying on an update. [d]
[f]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [2027 confirmed]
Do not upload a separate CV for either programme: the application form collects the relevant CV information
and an uploaded CV will be removed. Complete the form’s employment, research and other experience fields
instead. [a] [b]
Statement of purpose [2027 confirmed]
Required in English. DPhil maximum 800 words: faithful paraphrase of prompt - explain motivation, relevant
education/experience, research aptitude and intended areas and/or a research-plan outline. OMMS maximum

600 words: faithful paraphrase - explain motivation for Oxford, relevant educational/other background and
areas or specialization of interest. Display the word count if possible. Upload as a supporting document using
the accepted file formats; no special font/margin rule was found. [a] [b] [g]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
An optional contextual statement of up to 200 words allows relevant circumstances affecting opportunity or
attainment (for example first-generation background, caring, disadvantage, disability or displacement). Follow
the course’s Apply-section contextual-form link. This differs from the separate extenuating-circumstances
process. No compulsory generic personal/background essay is listed. [a] [b] [h]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
DPhil: required research-group indication in the form and intended interests in the 800-word statement;
specific dissertation title is not required. OMMS: preferred subject grouping in the form and interests within the
600-word statement. A separate research-interest essay is not listed. [a] [b]
Research proposal [Standing rule]
A full separate research proposal is not required by the mathematics DPhil checklist; research direction or a
plan outline belongs within the statement. OMMS has no listed proposal requirement. Separate
scholarship-specific requirements remain award dependent. [a] [b] [n]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Neither public checklist requests a writing sample, thesis or separate research summary. Publications are not
expected. Permission to upload/link unsolicited papers is not established; follow the live application fields. [a]
[b]
Publications list [Standing rule]
Publications are not expected; relevant research achievements may be recorded in the application form. A
separate publications-list upload is not listed, and paper upload versus link permissions were not publicly
established. [a] [b]
Course-list document [Standing rule]
No separate mathematics-course-list writing requirement is listed. Provide transcripts and academic
background in the prescribed fields. [a] [b]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
Clarendon: automatic consideration, no extra essay, application or supplementary documents. Other Oxford
and external scholarships have separate rules and may require forms or essays; the A-Z directory is the
controlling starting point, not a single universal scholarship prompt. Complete scholarship-specific checks once
nationality and awards are selected. [k] [n]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
DPhil proposed-field section must identify at least one research group, with optional supervisor names; OMMS
asks a preferred subject grouping. The publicly described contextual form is optional and limited to 200 words.
Portal-only short answers beyond the published guidance were not inspected. [a] [b] [h]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
No universally guaranteed mathematics funding amount was established. Clarendon covers course fees and a
living grant: its applicant page still illustrates at least £20,780 for 2025-26. Oxford’s living-cost page gives
£21,805 as the 2026-27 UKRI-linked graduate scholarship rate. Neither is a confirmed 2027-28 award amount;
the offer is controlling. Do not confuse a scholarship rate with automatic funding on admission. [k] [l]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Clarendon normally covers the course fee-liability period; continuation charges are excluded. Additional

maintenance beyond that period may depend on divisional policy. Course lengths are normally DPhil three to
four years and OMMS nine months; an award letter specifies funded duration. [a] [b] [k]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Clarendon is open to all nationalities and full-time/part-time eligible graduate subjects; overseas fees are
covered for recipients. Other awards may restrict citizenship or residence. F-1 status alone does not establish
eligibility for any nationality-restricted award. [k] [n]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Clarendon selection is competitive and not an automatic admission benefit. Award terms, course duration and
fee-liability rules govern support. DPhil students undertake a small teaching requirement with training and
payment; that is not a published universal full-funding guarantee. [a] [k]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Submit the course application by the relevant January funding deadline for automatic Clarendon consideration.
Other listed scholarships may require separate selection or applications; check the award’s own page and
deadlines. [k] [n]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Oxford’s 2027-28 scholarships A-Z and college awards are additional routes. Departmental studentships and
externally funded research projects may also exist. A current Francis Brown profile advertises ERC
Mathematics of Scattering Amplitudes PhD positions and requests the Mathematical Physics research-group
route; a specific 2027 opening/award amount was not independently confirmed. [n] [o] [fb]
Application fee [2027 confirmed]
DPhil research application £20; OMMS taught application £75, payable in GBP by Visa or Mastercard at
submission unless a waiver is granted. Fees are non-refundable. [i]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
Potential routes include qualifying low-income-country ordinary residence with inability to pay and academic
eligibility; refugee/displacement circumstances; eligible UK low-income applicants; and UNIQ+ participation.
Certain previously paid eligible CDT applications can enable additional related MPLS DPhil applications.
UChicago attendance or international/F-1 status alone is not a waiver category. Follow the relevant form, and
allow at least two weeks where the waiver route instructs it. [j]

University of Oxford
United Kingdom · DPhil in Mathematics; MSc in Mathematical Sciences (OMMS)
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• No separate CV upload: Oxford removes it.
• DPhil funding deadline is nearly two months before the expected final academic deadline.
• No automatic English waiver: request it; current TOEFL format restriction matters if waiver is refused.
• Scholarships are competitive; a DPhil offer is not by itself evidence of full funding.
• Current official rosters label Wiles, Kirwan and Hitchin emeritus.
• Oxford’s January deadlines are noon UK, not midnight.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [2027 confirmed]
Both programmes accept an appropriate first-class-equivalent bachelor’s; the normal minimum for a US degree
is 3.7/4.0. A master’s is not categorically required for the DPhil. A UChicago mathematics bachelor’s can
therefore meet the degree-route requirement, conditional on grades, preparation and completion before entry.
F-1 status is not a nationality or funding entitlement. DPhil 3-4 years; OMMS nine months. Both begin 4 October
2027. [a] [b]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select DPhil versus OMMS and create the Oxford graduate application. DPhil: name at least one research group
in the proposed-field section; up to three supervisors may be suggested, without prior approval. OMMS: choose
a preferred subject grouping; Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory, Topology and Logic is the closest initial
choice and does not bind later options. Register three referees; request English waiver in the form; prepare
transcripts and the programme-specific statement. [a] [b] [c] [d]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
DPhil applicants need not obtain a supervisor’s agreement before applying; up to three names may be
suggested and academic contact is permitted. OMMS does not require a prospective supervisor. Current
rosters list Wiles, Kirwan, Hitchin and several historically prominent names as emeritus; do not treat them as
ordinary new-supervisor options without confirmation. The faculty below are a research-fit shortlist, not a
guarantee of 2027 availability. [a] [b] [p] [q] [r]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use Oxford’s online form and Applicant Self Service. Register referees before submission if desired; track
receipt after submission. Required documents use PDF/JPG/PNG and normal 4 MB maximum. Do not upload a
CV where the course forbids it. Live unpublished form questions and already-submitted-reference replacement
behavior remain unverified. [d] [e] [f] [g]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Both course pages explicitly publish 2027-28 entry dates and deadlines. General mechanics are standing
guidance. The stated scholarship-rate figures are prior-year examples, not 2027-28 promises. [a] [b] [k] [l]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
DPhil: 6 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time is the funding deadline; expected final deadline 2 March 2027 at
12:00 noon UK time, subject to places. OMMS: final deadline 27 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time. These are
midday, not midnight. [a] [b]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
DPhil funding consideration: 6 January 2027 noon UK. OMMS funding consideration: 27 January 2027 noon UK.
Clarendon automatically considers eligible course applications received by the relevant December/January
course deadline; other awards can impose their own deadlines. [a] [b] [k] [n]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
Register three referees. The application can become ready for assessment with two references received by the
relevant course deadline; Oxford may require the third before completing review. For safety request all three
by DPhil 6 January 2027 noon UK or OMMS 27 January 2027 noon UK when seeking funding. The deadline
entered by the applicant appears in the invitation and does not extend Oxford’s deadline. [a] [b] [d] [e]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
No GRE scores are sought. English evidence need not necessarily accompany the initial application: if a waiver
is refused, the individual offer specifies the condition and deadline. No universal 2027 test-score deadline was
established. [a] [b] [c] [m]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All required application materials must arrive by the selected course deadline, except English evidence where
permitted as a later offer condition. Submit early enough to correct format/missing-document problems.
Final-degree and other offer conditions have individualized deadlines. [a] [b] [c] [g] [m]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The department’s offer specifies the acceptance deadline and conditions; no uniform US-style April 15
commitment deadline applies. College financial declarations can have a separate deadline. [m]
English and GRE
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
DPhil uses standard English: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 each component. OMMS uses higher
English: IELTS 7.5 overall, at least 7.0 each. Published TOEFL thresholds are 100 and 110 respectively, each
requiring listening 22, reading 24, speaking 25, writing 24, BUT both current course pages say TOEFL tests
taken from 21 January 2026 are not accepted pending review of the revised test. Consult the current official
table before booking. [a] [b]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A waiver can be requested for a completed or current full-time degree of at least nine months taught and
assessed entirely in English, with no more than two academic years between completion and Oxford entry.
UChicago falls within the US/majority-English-country route: additional medium-of-instruction evidence is not
normally required. Select the waiver request in the Languages section; the department decides, so it is not an
automatic exemption. Completion of the qualifying degree can be a condition. [c]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Neither course seeks GRE or GMAT scores. No separate Mathematics Subject Test requirement is listed; do not
add unsolicited scores as a substitute for the stated materials. [a] [b]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload official institutional transcripts showing individual grades; current students use the available transcript,
with final degree evidence later if required. Documents not in English need certified translations. General
upload formats are PDF/JPG/PNG up to 4 MB; separate instructions cover documents of 4-10 MB. [a] [b] [g]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
DPhil: three referees, preferably academic; up to one professional reference can be accepted. OMMS: three, at
least two academic. In both cases Oxford may begin assessment with two received, while retaining the right to
require the third. [a] [b] [d]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Clarendon requires no separate application documents or references. Other named scholarships can require
additional material; citizenship-specific awards cannot be fully resolved without nationality. No universal
supplementary scholarship-reference requirement applies. [k] [n]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Registering a referee sends an email invitation immediately. Use institutional/professional email where
possible and enter a realistic deadline. The referee completes short questions and uploads a PDF reference. [e]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not held until application submission. The application may be submitted before references
arrive; each course application requires its own registered references. [d] [e]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Applicant Self Service displays reference status; Oxford emails the applicant when a reference is received. The
referee receives on-screen and email confirmation after submitting. [e] [f]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Self Service permits referee changes/additions and reminder/resend actions subject to the application state.
References must be registered/submitted separately for each application. Whether a submitted letter can be
replaced by the referee was not established publicly: ask graduate admissions before relying on an update. [d]

instead. [a] [b]

education/experience, research aptitude and intended areas and/or a research-plan outline. OMMS maximum

Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
An optional contextual statement of up to 200 words allows relevant circumstances affecting opportunity or

University of Oxford
United Kingdom · DPhil in Mathematics; MSc in Mathematical Sciences (OMMS)
Relevant European programme; no numerical ranking asserted
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• No separate CV upload: Oxford removes it.
• DPhil funding deadline is nearly two months before the expected final academic deadline.
• No automatic English waiver: request it; current TOEFL format restriction matters if waiver is refused.
• Scholarships are competitive; a DPhil offer is not by itself evidence of full funding.
• Current official rosters label Wiles, Kirwan and Hitchin emeritus.
• Oxford’s January deadlines are noon UK, not midnight.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [2027 confirmed]
Both programmes accept an appropriate first-class-equivalent bachelor’s; the normal minimum for a US degree
is 3.7/4.0. A master’s is not categorically required for the DPhil. A UChicago mathematics bachelor’s can
therefore meet the degree-route requirement, conditional on grades, preparation and completion before entry.
F-1 status is not a nationality or funding entitlement. DPhil 3-4 years; OMMS nine months. Both begin 4 October
2027. [a] [b]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Select DPhil versus OMMS and create the Oxford graduate application. DPhil: name at least one research group
in the proposed-field section; up to three supervisors may be suggested, without prior approval. OMMS: choose
a preferred subject grouping; Algebra, Geometry, Number Theory, Topology and Logic is the closest initial
choice and does not bind later options. Register three referees; request English waiver in the form; prepare
transcripts and the programme-specific statement. [a] [b] [c] [d]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
DPhil applicants need not obtain a supervisor’s agreement before applying; up to three names may be
suggested and academic contact is permitted. OMMS does not require a prospective supervisor. Current
rosters list Wiles, Kirwan, Hitchin and several historically prominent names as emeritus; do not treat them as
ordinary new-supervisor options without confirmation. The faculty below are a research-fit shortlist, not a
guarantee of 2027 availability. [a] [b] [p] [q] [r]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use Oxford’s online form and Applicant Self Service. Register referees before submission if desired; track
receipt after submission. Required documents use PDF/JPG/PNG and normal 4 MB maximum. Do not upload a
CV where the course forbids it. Live unpublished form questions and already-submitted-reference replacement
behavior remain unverified. [d] [e] [f] [g]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Both course pages explicitly publish 2027-28 entry dates and deadlines. General mechanics are standing
guidance. The stated scholarship-rate figures are prior-year examples, not 2027-28 promises. [a] [b] [k] [l]

Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
DPhil: 6 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time is the funding deadline; expected final deadline 2 March 2027 at
12:00 noon UK time, subject to places. OMMS: final deadline 27 January 2027 at 12:00 noon UK time. These are
midday, not midnight. [a] [b]
Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
DPhil funding consideration: 6 January 2027 noon UK. OMMS funding consideration: 27 January 2027 noon UK.
Clarendon automatically considers eligible course applications received by the relevant December/January
course deadline; other awards can impose their own deadlines. [a] [b] [k] [n]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
Register three referees. The application can become ready for assessment with two references received by the
relevant course deadline; Oxford may require the third before completing review. For safety request all three
by DPhil 6 January 2027 noon UK or OMMS 27 January 2027 noon UK when seeking funding. The deadline
entered by the applicant appears in the invitation and does not extend Oxford’s deadline. [a] [b] [d] [e]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
No GRE scores are sought. English evidence need not necessarily accompany the initial application: if a waiver
is refused, the individual offer specifies the condition and deadline. No universal 2027 test-score deadline was
established. [a] [b] [c] [m]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All required application materials must arrive by the selected course deadline, except English evidence where
permitted as a later offer condition. Submit early enough to correct format/missing-document problems.
Final-degree and other offer conditions have individualized deadlines. [a] [b] [c] [g] [m]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
The department’s offer specifies the acceptance deadline and conditions; no uniform US-style April 15
commitment deadline applies. College financial declarations can have a separate deadline. [m]
English and GRE
English requirement [2027 confirmed]
DPhil uses standard English: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall, at least 6.5 each component. OMMS uses higher
English: IELTS 7.5 overall, at least 7.0 each. Published TOEFL thresholds are 100 and 110 respectively, each
requiring listening 22, reading 24, speaking 25, writing 24, BUT both current course pages say TOEFL tests
taken from 21 January 2026 are not accepted pending review of the revised test. Consult the current official
table before booking. [a] [b]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A waiver can be requested for a completed or current full-time degree of at least nine months taught and
assessed entirely in English, with no more than two academic years between completion and Oxford entry.
UChicago falls within the US/majority-English-country route: additional medium-of-instruction evidence is not
normally required. Select the waiver request in the Languages section; the department decides, so it is not an
automatic exemption. Completion of the qualifying degree can be a condition. [c]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [2027 confirmed]
Neither course seeks GRE or GMAT scores. No separate Mathematics Subject Test requirement is listed; do not
add unsolicited scores as a substitute for the stated materials. [a] [b]

Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload official institutional transcripts showing individual grades; current students use the available transcript,
with final degree evidence later if required. Documents not in English need certified translations. General
upload formats are PDF/JPG/PNG up to 4 MB; separate instructions cover documents of 4-10 MB. [a] [b] [g]
Mathematics-course list [Standing rule]
No separate mathematics-course list is specified in either course’s supporting-document checklist. Degree and
academic-history fields and transcripts still record preparation; a portal-only additional requirement was not
independently inspected. [a] [b]
Course descriptions [Standing rule]
Separate course descriptions or syllabi are not listed as required documents on the public course pages.
Submission permissions for unsolicited syllabi were not established. [a] [b]
Recommendation letters
Number and type [Standing rule]
DPhil: three referees, preferably academic; up to one professional reference can be accepted. OMMS: three, at
least two academic. In both cases Oxford may begin assessment with two received, while retaining the right to
require the third. [a] [b] [d]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
Clarendon requires no separate application documents or references. Other named scholarships can require
additional material; citizenship-specific awards cannot be fully resolved without nationality. No universal
supplementary scholarship-reference requirement applies. [k] [n]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Registering a referee sends an email invitation immediately. Use institutional/professional email where
possible and enter a realistic deadline. The referee completes short questions and uploads a PDF reference. [e]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations are not held until application submission. The application may be submitted before references
arrive; each course application requires its own registered references. [d] [e]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Applicant Self Service displays reference status; Oxford emails the applicant when a reference is received. The
referee receives on-screen and email confirmation after submitting. [e] [f]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Self Service permits referee changes/additions and reminder/resend actions subject to the application state.
References must be registered/submitted separately for each application. Whether a submitted letter can be
replaced by the referee was not established publicly: ask graduate admissions before relying on an update. [d]
[f]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [2027 confirmed]
Do not upload a separate CV for either programme: the application form collects the relevant CV information
and an uploaded CV will be removed. Complete the form’s employment, research and other experience fields
instead. [a] [b]
Statement of purpose [2027 confirmed]
Required in English. DPhil maximum 800 words: faithful paraphrase of prompt - explain motivation, relevant
education/experience, research aptitude and intended areas and/or a research-plan outline. OMMS maximum

600 words: faithful paraphrase - explain motivation for Oxford, relevant educational/other background and
areas or specialization of interest. Display the word count if possible. Upload as a supporting document using
the accepted file formats; no special font/margin rule was found. [a] [b] [g]
Personal / background statement [Standing rule]
An optional contextual statement of up to 200 words allows relevant circumstances affecting opportunity or
attainment (for example first-generation background, caring, disadvantage, disability or displacement). Follow
the course’s Apply-section contextual-form link. This differs from the separate extenuating-circumstances
process. No compulsory generic personal/background essay is listed. [a] [b] [h]
Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
DPhil: required research-group indication in the form and intended interests in the 800-word statement;
specific dissertation title is not required. OMMS: preferred subject grouping in the form and interests within the
600-word statement. A separate research-interest essay is not listed. [a] [b]
